dataset.name: real WANDS catalog (1x) + Phase 6B's own controlled-stress replication ladder (2x/5x/10x/20x, up to 859,880 products), same 7 category_depth_1 checkpoints

engine_config.solr: Apache Solr 9.10.1, wands_bench + wands_bench_2x/_5x/_10x/_20x cores (Phase 6B's own)

headline_result.correctness_gate: 85/85 count-match checks (17 rows x 5 tiers) and 35/35 top-50-facet exact matches against live Solr cores, zero mismatches
headline_result.ordinal_vs_solr_35_of_35_checkpoint_tier: faster at every combination across the whole 1x-20x range (2,002-320,780 candidates), 2.5x-72.6x, zero exceptions
headline_result.finding: the ordinal method's advantage over Solr holds across the entire tested scale range but is NOT scale-invariant -- it narrows (not grows) at the largest candidate counts, converging toward roughly 2.5x-3x rather than an ever-widening advantage; the mirror-image trend (margin over the scan method growing sharply with scale) is mechanistically consistent with the scan method's per-candidate BTreeMap-clone cost getting relatively worse at scale
headline_result.named_limitation: single-run-per-tier (not 3-repeated-full-binary); only color facet tested; scale ladder holds facet cardinality fixed by design (Phase 6B's own disclosed choice), so organic (not just candidate-count) growth beyond 320,780 candidates is untested
